p: If you've never done anything like this before, here's what to expect when you arrive. You'll check in, get a harness fitted by the staff, then sit through a short safety briefing on how to clip in and out of the auto-belays. After that, it's over to you for the rest of the session. It's all very straightforward, but it does take a few minutes, so arrive early.

Have the paperwork done before you go. Every climber needs a participation form, signed by a parent or guardian for under-18s, and it's quicker filled in online. Check the age guidance when you book, as there's usually a minimum age for climbers and supervision rules for younger children.

Allow a couple of hours for the whole visit. A light snack beforehand, a water bottle and comfy clothes are all you need. Climb with your legs, not just your arms, and you'll last longer on the walls.

Newcastle is packed with things to do afterwards. The Great North Museum: Hancock has dinosaurs, a planetarium and lots of hands-on bits, and it's free. The Discovery Museum, near the station, tells the story of Tyneside's inventors and shipbuilders. Life Science Centre is great for curious kids, and Jesmond Dene, a wooded valley with a little river and Pets' Corner, makes a lovely green escape on the edge of the city.
